issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradictory parameter type for addGuestStudents: one textual instruction says addGuestStudents(String) while the UML and the provided solution use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected parameter type and how to implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the textual task description in problem_statement.md to match the UML and solution by specifying addGuestStudents(int). Clarify that the method takes an integer number of new guest students to add. Ensure the template TODO refers to the int parameter so students implement the correct signature.

issues.description: The problem statement text specifies addGuestStudents(String) (a String parameter) while the UML diagram and the reference implementation use addGuestStudents(int) (an int parameter). This mismatch in the expected method signature for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) can confuse students about the correct parameter type to implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across artifacts. Preferably update the problem statement to declare addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML and the solution, or alternatively change the UML and solution to use a String if there is a strong reason to accept numeric input as text. Ensure all places (problem text, UML, template comments, and solution) use the same signature: addGuestStudents(int).
